<h>Reading 1</h>
Continuation of the Holy Gospel according to Luke
<r>Luke 3:1-6</r>
<c>I</c>n the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea. And so on.

Homily by Pope St. Gregory <n>the Great.</n>
<r>10th on the Gospels.</r>
<c>T</c>he date, at which the Fore-runner of our Redeemer entered on his public office of preaching, is indicated to us by the name of the ruler of the Roman Commonwealth, and by those of the princes of Palestine. The time of his preaching is indicated by these names, because he came as the Fore-runner of Him Who was to be the Redeemer of some Jews and many Gentiles. Moreover in the enumeration of these worldly monarchs there is a foreshadowing of the fact, that the Gentiles were about to be gathered into one, and the Jews to be scattered abroad in punishment of their unbelief; in the whole heathen Commonwealth we find the title of one Emperor, but in the small kingdom of Judaea are mentioned four masters.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Send forth the Lamb, O Lord, the Ruler of the land; from the rock in the wilderness unto the mount of the daughter of Zion.
<r>℣.</r> Ex Sion spécies decóris ejus: Deus noster véniet.
* From the rock in the wilderness unto the mount of the daughter of Zion.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<c>Q</c>uia autem gentílitas colligénda erat, et Iudǽa pro culpa perfídiæ dispergénda, ipsa quoque descríptio terréni principátus osténdit: quóniam et in Romána república unus præfuísse descríbitur, et in Iudǽæ regno per quartam partem plúrimi principabántur. Voce étenim nostri Redemptóris dícitur: Omne regnum in seípsum divisum desolábitur. Liquet ergo, quod ad finem regni Iudǽa pervénerat, quæ tot régibus divísa subiacébat.

<h>Reading 2</h>
Continuation of the Holy Gospel according to Luke
<r>Luke 3:1-6</r>
<c>I</c>n the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea. And so on.

Homily by Pope St. Gregory <n>the Great.</n>
<r>10th on the Gospels.</r>
<c>T</c>he date, at which the Fore-runner of our Redeemer entered on his public office of preaching, is indicated to us by the name of the ruler of the Roman Commonwealth, and by those of the princes of Palestine. The time of his preaching is indicated by these names, because he came as the Fore-runner of Him Who was to be the Redeemer of some Jews and many Gentiles. Moreover in the enumeration of these worldly monarchs there is a foreshadowing of the fact, that the Gentiles were about to be gathered into one, and the Jews to be scattered abroad in punishment of their unbelief; in the whole heathen Commonwealth we find the title of one Emperor, but in the small kingdom of Judaea are mentioned four masters. The blessed voice of the Saviour itself hath said, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation <n>Luke xi. 17.</n> And we may well look for the ruin of the Jewish state when we see it divided among so many rulers. We observe likewise that the names of the reigning priests as well as kings are given. The Evangelist Luke hath left on record the chiefs both of the monarchy and of the priesthood who held office when John the Baptist began to preach, because John preached Him Who is at once our Priest and our King.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> The waste places have brought forth sweet-smelling buds for Israel; for, behold, our God will come with power.
* And His brightness is with Him.
<r>℣.</r> Ecce dominátor Dóminus cum virtúte véniet.
<r>℟.</r> And His brightness is with Him.

Et venit in omnem regiónem Iordánis, prǽdicans baptísmum pœniténtiæ in remissiónem peccatórum.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uartodécimo Kaléndas Ianuárii Luna vicésima prima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>I</h>n Mauritánia sancti Timóthei Diáconi, qui ob Christi fidem, post diros cárceres, in ignem coniéctus, martýrium consummávit.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ beáti Nemésii Mártyris, qui, primo per calúmniam quasi latro Iúdici delátus, eoque crímine absolútus, mox, in persecutióne Décii, Christiánæ religiónis nómine accusátus Æmiliáno Iúdici; a quo, geminátis supplíciis excruciátus, cum latrónibus iussus est incéndi, Salvatóris déferens similitúdinem, qui una cum latrónibus pértulit crucem.
<h>N</h>icǽæ, in Bithýnia, sanctórum Mártyrum Dárii, Zósimi, Pauli et Secúndi.
<h>N</h>icomedíæ sanctórum Mártyrum Cyríaci, Paulílli, Secúndi, Anastásii, Syndímii et Sociórum.
<h>G</h>azæ, in Palæstína, pássio sanctárum Meuris et Theæ.
<h>R</h>omæ deposítio sancti Anastásii Papæ Primi, viri ditíssimæ paupertátis et apostólicæ sollicitúdinis, quem (ut ait sanctus Hierónymus) diu Roma habére non méruit, ne orbis caput sub tali Epíscopo truncarétur; nam, haud multo post eius óbitum, Roma a Gothis capta et dirépta fuit.
<h>A</h>ntisiodóri sancti Gregórii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>A</h>ureliánis, in Gállia, sancti Adiúti Abbátis, prophético spíritu illústris.
<h>R</h>omæ sanctæ Faustæ, quæ fuit mater sanctæ Anastásiæ, ac nobilitáte et pietáte éxstitit insígnis.
<h>A</h>venióne beáti Urbáni Papæ Quinti, qui, Sede Apostólica Romæ restitúta, Græcórum cum Latínis coniunctióne perfécta, infidélibus coércitis, de Ecclésia óptime méritus est. Eius cultum pervetústum Pius Nonus, Póntifex Máximus, ratum hábuit et confirmávit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.edc483996d:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>D</c>ecember 19th 2027, the 21st day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>I</h>n Morocco, (in the fourth century,) the holy martyr Timothy, the Deacon, who after a terrible imprisonment was cast into the fire for Christ's faith's sake, and so finished his testimony.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, in Egypt, the blessed martyr Nemesius. He was first brought before the judge on a false accusation that he was a thief, and was acquitted but in the persecution under the Emperor Decius he was accused of Christianity before the judge Aemilian, by whom he was put to the double punishment and condemned to be burnt along with thieves. In the which thing he was conformed to the likeness of the Saviour, who was crucified between thieves.
<h>A</h>t Nice, (now Isnik, in Bithynia,) the holy martyrs Darius, Zosimus, Paul, and Secundus, (in the fourth century.)
<h>A</h>t Nicomedia, the holy martyrs Cyriacus, Paulillus, Secundus, Anastasius, Syndimius, and their Companions, (in the fourth century.)
<h>A</h>t Gaza, in Palestine, (in the third century,) the holy martyrs Meuris and Thea.
<h>A</h>t Rome, blessed Pope Anastasius [I, in the year 401,] a man very rich in poverty and apostolic care, of whom St. Jerome writeth that Rome deserved not long to have him, lest the head of the world should be cut off under such a Bishop, since no long while after his death Rome was taken and sacked by the Goths.
<h>A</h>t Auxerre, the holy Confessor Gregory, (looked on as 12th) Bishop (of that see, successor of St. Theodore, in the year 530.)
<h>A</h>t Orleans, the holy Abbot Adjutus, famous for the spirit of prophecy.
<h>A</h>t Rome, holy Fausta, the mother of holy Anastasia, eminent for her rank and godliness, (at the end of the third century.)
<h>A</h>t Avignon, the blessed Pope Urban V, who performed the highest service to the Church; he restored the Apostolic seat to Rome, he completed the union of the Greeks and the Latins, he brought the unbelievers into subjection. His very ancient veneration was ratified and confirmed by Pope Pius IX.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

b.7eebf64c50:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Ier 23:5</r>
<c>E</c>cce dies véniunt, dicit Dóminus, et suscitábo David germen iustum: et regnábit rex, et sápiens erit: et fáciet iudícium et iustítiam in terra.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Non auferétur sceptrum de Iuda, et dux de fémore eius, donec véniat qui mitténdus est:
* Et ipse erit exspectátio géntium.
<r>℣.</r> Pulchrióres sunt óculi eius vino, et dentes eius lacte candidióres.
<r>℟.</r> Et ipse erit exspectátio géntium.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Et ipse erit exspectátio géntium.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>C</c>ónditor alme síderum,
Ætérna lux credéntium,
Christe, Redémptor ómnium,
Exáudi preces súpplicum.

<h>Q</h>ui cóndolens intéritu
Mortis períre sǽculum,
Salvásti mundum lánguidum,
Donans reis remédium,

<h>V</h>ergénte mundi véspere,
Uti sponsus de thálamo,
Egréssus honestíssima
Vírginis matris cláusula.

<h>C</h>uius forti poténtiæ
Genu curvántur ómnia;
Cæléstia, terréstria
Nutu faténtur súbdita.

<h>T</h>e deprecámur, hágie,
Ventúre iudex sǽculi,
Consérva nos in témpore
Hostis a telo pérfidi.

<h>L</h>aus, honor, virtus, glória,
Deo Patri, et Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Roráte, cæli, désuper, et nubes pluant iustum.
<r>℟.</r> Aperiátur terra, et gérminet Salvatórem.
b.cb421f03bb:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Jer 23:5</r>
<c>B</c>ehold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will raise up to David a just branch: and a king shall reign, and shall be wise, and shall execute judgement and justice in the earth.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor the law-giver from his loins, until he that shall be sent cometh.
* And unto him shall the longing of the Gentiles be.
<r>℣.</r> His eyes shall be bright with wine, and his teeth white with milk.
<r>℟.</r> And unto him shall the desire of the Gentiles be.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> And unto him shall the desire of the Gentiles be.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>B</c>right builder of the heavenly poles,
Eternal light of faithful souls,
Jesus, Redeemer of mankind,
Our humble prayers vouchsafe to mind.

<h>W</h>ho, lest the fraud of hell’s black king
Should all men to destruction bring,
Didst, by an act of generous love,
The fainting world’s physician prove.

<h>W</h>ho, that thou mightst our ransom pay
And wash the stains of sin away,
Wouldst from a Virgin’s womb proceed
And on the cross a victim bleed.

<h>W</h>hose glorious power, whose saving name
No sooner any voice can frame,
But heaven and earth and hell agree
To honour them with trembling knee.

<h>T</h>hee, Christ, who at the latter day
Shalt be our Judge, we humbly pray
Such arms of heavenly grace to send
As may thy Church from foes defend.

<h>B</h>e glory given and honour done
To God the Father and the Son
And to the Holy Ghost on high,
From age to age eternally.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Drop down dew, ye heavens, from above, and let the clouds rain the Just.
<r>℟.</r> Let the earth be opened, and bud forth the Saviour.
